claims.claim: The existing agenda-page repertoire write handlers (handleAddWork, handleStatusChange, handlePinEdition, handleRemoveItem) are hardcoded to currentSeasonId and operate over the per-event worksByEventId map (via findRow/patchRow), not a standalone season-repertoire list, so they cannot be reused verbatim for a manageableSeasonId-scoped panel section

A repertoire section listing manageableSeasonId's items (which may differ from currentSeasonId, or exist when no agenda event references them) needs its own state + handler functions, following the shape of event/[id]/+page.svelte's loadManagePickers/loadComposeSurfaces (which correctly parameterize on `sid`/`loaded.seasonId` rather than a page global) as the closer precedent, or new season-manage-local equivalents.

claims.claim: Rights gating for the new section needs no new rights read: the whole season-manage panel is already gated on manageableSeasonRights === 'editor' (showSeasonManageGear), so a repertoire section inside it can render unconditionally under that existing gate, matching the issue's 'reuse the rights that gate the repertoire surface today' instruction once read as 'editor on the managed season' rather than literally reusing the currentSeasonId-scoped seasonManageRights state

risks: Wiring the repertoire section needs a new manageableSeasonId-scoped fetch (listRepertoireItems + listWorks + listAllEditions + listAllCopies, or reuse of collective-wide libraryWorks/libraryEditions plus a fresh listAllCopies call) inside openSeasonManagePanel — this is 3-4 new network requests on every panel open that don't exist today; worth sizing against the panel's existing already-heavy open cost (roster + sections + series + events).

New parallel state + write handlers are needed for the section (its own WorkRow[] list, patchRow/findRow-equivalent, handleAddWork/handleRemoveItem scoped to manageableSeasonId) since the existing agenda handlers are hardcoded to currentSeasonId and the per-event worksByEventId cache — this is real new surface, not just a template drop-in, contrary to a naive reading of 'reusing RepertoireElement if it drops in'.

The issue's rights wording ('same rights that gate the repertoire surface today') is ambiguous between the currentSeasonId-scoped seasonManageRights and the panel's own manageableSeasonRights; manageableSeasonRights is read here as correct (it's already the panel's gate and avoids hiding the section for a future-only manageable season with no current season running), but this is a judgment call not settled by the issue text alone and should be confirmed with the implementing engineer/Gama rather than assumed silently. [speculative]

buildWorkRows requires the whole-collective works/editions/copies lookup sets (collectSources) even for a season-only list — reusing +page.svelte's existing libraryWorks/libraryEditions (already loaded for the agenda picker, collective-wide so season-agnostic) is safe to share, but listAllCopies is not currently loaded anywhere on +page.svelte and would be a genuinely new call.

Per the issue's 'Done when' item 3, the per-event 'repertoire'-context fallback rows must keep rendering unchanged — the new section is additive; care is needed that its own optimistic writes (create/delete of repertoire_item) also refresh/invalidate the agenda's separate worksByEventId fallback rows so the two surfaces don't drift out of sync after a panel-side add/remove (mirrors the event-detail page's existing dual-refresh pattern in refreshWorks, which already re-reads both loadWorksByEventId and listRepertoireItems after a write — a reusable precedent).

risks: Design gap not yet resolved by anyone: the new repertoire section will live inside a panel gated on manageableSeasonRights/manageableSeasonId, but per Done-when 4 it must itself gate on seasonManageRights (keyed to a possibly-different currentSeasonId/seasonId). No test and no code today exercises 'panel open, repertoire section rights absent' — needs an explicit design answer (render nothing? a locked/empty state? which season's repertoire does it even show if manageableSeasonId != currentSeasonId?) before implementation, not just a rights-check bolted on.

If Done-when 4's suggested approach (reuse RepertoireElement in 'repertoire' context inside the panel) is taken literally, it will produce duplicate `data-testid` nodes (work-manage-add-work, work-manage-remove, work-status-*, work-row, etc.) on the same page whenever an unprogrammed event's fallback row is visible at the same time as the open panel. Several existing specs assert on these testids via unscoped `container.querySelector`/`querySelectorAll` with exact-length checks (repertoire-manage-wiring.spec.ts, event/[id]/page.spec.ts) — those will need to be scoped (e.g. `within('[data-testid=season-manage-panel]')` vs `within('[data-testid=agenda-...]')`) as part of this change, or the new section needs distinct testids, otherwise green tests could start silently asserting against the wrong instance.

ADMIN_TESTIDS (page.agenda-admin.spec.ts:364-374) sweeps the panel as one opaque unit and will pass trivially for the 'no rights anywhere' scenario without any change. But no fail-closed sweep exists (or is proposed) for the divergent scenario — manageable-season rights present (panel visible) but repertoire rights absent — which is exactly the case this issue's rights model can produce. That's a coverage gap the implementer should close with a new test, independent of whether ADMIN_TESTIDS itself needs a new literal entry.

claims.claim: #222's keyboard-roving toolbar and RepertoireElement's own per-row status toolbar cannot cross-contaminate: both keydown handlers scope querySelectorAll to their own e.currentTarget, and the season-manage-panel div is a DOM SIBLING of the role="toolbar" header div (not nested inside it).

No shared ancestor queries either group; adding a repertoire section inside the panel cannot join the header's roving walk.

risks: Real testid-collision risk: if the panel mounts RepertoireElement with expanded=true (the event/[id] precedent for management surfaces), opening the panel plus expanding any one unprogrammed event's own works line elsewhere in the same agenda renders duplicate data-testid values (work-row, work-status-{value}, work-status-group-{row.id}, work-manage-*) for the same repertoire_item ids on the page simultaneously. This will break any spec/assertion using page-level getByTestId without container scoping, and is a genuine (if narrower) pre-existing risk today across two-or-more simultaneously-expanded unprogrammed-event rows even before #234 — #234 makes it trivially reachable via panel-open + one click. Flag as a required review-checklist item: either scope test queries to a container, or accept/document the duplication.

If the implementation adds a new dedicated state variable (e.g. a cached season-repertoire WorkRow[] array) rather than deriving rows inline from existing seasonRepertoire/libraryWorks/libraryEditions, that variable must be added to resetManagement() (+page.svelte:954-966) or stale rows from the previous collective will persist visibly in the panel until the next async load resolves.

listAllCopies is not currently fetched by loadManagePickers (only by the per-event loadWorksByEventId) — omitting it for the panel's rows would silently drop the 'Borrow' link (canBorrow) on season-repertoire rows shown in the panel, a subtle correctness gap not caught by a green build.

The shared tree currently carries an uncommitted #222 F1 fix in +page.svelte at the exact {#if} line the panel hangs off of (the card's disclosure gate) plus an uncommitted spec change — this should land (commit) before or as part of #234's RED so #234's diff isn't built against a phantom/uncommitted baseline.
